Log-likelihood of one measurement under a trajectory

Source: R/likelihood.R
obs_loglik.Rd

Observations are modelled on the \(\log_{10}\) scale. A detected measurement contributes a normal density about the trajectory; a measurement below the assay limit contributes the corresponding tail probability, so left-censoring is handled exactly rather than by imputation.

Usage

obs_loglik(y, mu, sigma, lod = NULL, censored = FALSE, eps = 1e-12)

Arguments

y

Observed value on the natural (not log) scale.

mu

Trajectory value at the observation time, natural scale.

sigma

Residual standard deviation on the \(\log_{10}\) scale.

lod

Assay limit of detection, natural scale. Used only when censored is TRUE.

censored

Logical; TRUE if the measurement is below lod.

eps

Small constant guarding log10() against zero.

Value

A numeric vector of log-likelihood contributions.

Examples

obs_loglik(y = 1000, mu = 1200, sigma = 0.5)
#> [1] -0.2383307
obs_loglik(y = NA, mu = 50, sigma = 0.5, lod = 100, censored = TRUE)
#> [1] -0.3196092
